subject: Renewal: Pricing guardrail and path from Paygo to Commit
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@aerocart.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@aerocart.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal planning — looking to move from Paygo to Commit (pricing guardrails)

Ben,

We’re kicking off renewal planning for AeroCart (contract ends 2028-03-31) and want to explore moving from strict pay-as-you-go to a committed model for 2028. Two asks from procurement and the engineering leads: 1) can Redwood offer a firm price hold for 12 months to avoid mid-year reprice risk, and 2) we need protections for seasonal spikes so we don’t get locked into a large commit that’s wasted during Q3.

Specifically, they asked whether you can propose a path that:
- lets us start with a conservative commit (6–9 months) and step up if usage trends hit triggers
- includes credits for unused committed capacity (prefer roll-forward vs forfeiture)
- provides burst protection for unpredictable marketing spikes (90-day elevated burst window)

I’ve looped in procurement (bcc’d) — they’ll want the commercial/contract language for credits and any invoice treatment. Can you send us a concrete proposal and any SOW or pricing spreadsheet we can share with legal/procurement?

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of Platform Engineering, AeroCart
T: +1 415 555 0172

---
Attachment: none in this message
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@aerocart.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Dec 2027 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — looking to move from Paygo to Commit (pricing guardrails)

Tom — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear asks. I’ve sketched a proposal below that maps to the three points procurement asked about. I’m attaching an editable pricing model and a draft SOW for discussion.

High-level proposal (paygo -> commit path):
- Stage 1 (6 months): small committed baseline (20% of projected quarterly consumption) with a 15% unit discount vs current paygo list.
- Stage 2 (optional step-up): after 6 months, automatic review; if 4-week trailing usage > 85% of commit for two consecutive weeks, commit can be increased to a higher tier with a pre-agreed price (no reprice for 12 months).
- Credits & roll-forward: unused committed capacity converts to credits usable across next 2 quarters (cap 50% of unused).
- Burst protection: for the first 90 days after a signed commit, overages billed at a softened overage rate (paygo discounted by 20%) to reduce spike pain.
- Price hold: if AeroCart signs a 12-month commit, we’ll hold the agreed unit price for 12 months (no mid-term increases except for explicit regulatory taxes).

Options A/B/C (covered in attached spreadsheet) outline different commit levels and corresponding discounts and credit multipliers.

Next steps:
1) Kimberly — can you review margin impact and confirm the max burst allowance we can take on for Q1?
2) Tom & Procurement — if helpful I can run a short model showing billing scenarios for your busiest weeks.
3) If the terms look good, I’ll route to legal and send a DocuSign-ready SOW.

Link to HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/REDWOOD/record/123456
DocuSign preview will be provided once legal confirms redlines.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call next week.

— Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 650 555 0110

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Dec 2027 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: AeroCart — pricing guardrail options (margin check)

Team — pulling together notes after Ben’s initial proposal. Re-quoting Ben below for context.

> Stage 1 (6 months): small committed baseline (20% of projected quarterly consumption) with a 15% unit discount vs current paygo list.
> Stage 2 (optional step-up): after 6 months, automatic review; if 4-week trailing usage > 85% of commit for two consecutive weeks, commit can be increased to a higher tier with a pre-agreed price (no reprice for 12 months).
> Credits & roll-forward: unused committed capacity converts to credits usable across next 2 quarters (cap 50% of unused).
> Burst protection: first 90 days after sign, overages billed at softened overage rate (paygo discounted by 20%).
> Price hold: sign 12-month commit -> price held for 12 months.

Margin analysis (quick):
- Option A (conservative commit): ~12% reduction in gross margin for Q1/Q2 but protects ARR and reduces churn risk.
- Option B (moderate commit + step-up): ~7% margin hit first 6 months, recovers if they step up. This is our recommended commercial sweet spot.
- Option C (aggressive commit, deeper discount): ~3% margin impact long-term but higher ARR predictability.

Operational asks:
- Can we implement a simple roll-forward credit ledger tied to account billing (not a refund)? Finance needs to confirm invoice presentation.
- Legal: minor SOW redlines likely around data retention and audit logs; get these few clauses pre-approved to avoid friction.

Marissa — can you authorize Ben to offer Option B (moderate) with the following guardrail: 15% initial discount, 25% credit roll-forward cap, 12-month price hold once they sign 12 months? If yes, I’ll finalize the language for the SOW and run it through David for invoice presentation.

Thanks,
Kimberly

Subject: Re: Renewal planning — pricing guardrail and path from Paygo to Commit (final commercial)

Tom — thanks for the patience. Below is the commercial we can present to procurement and legal. We ran the margin/legal checks internally and are ready to proceed if AeroCart confirms.

Final commercial (Option B — recommended):
- Term: 12 months (start on signature)
- Initial commit: 20% of projected quarterly consumption (applied monthly)
- Pricing: 15% unit discount vs current paygo list for committed units
- Price hold: agreed unit price held for 12 months from signature (excludes taxes and third-party pass-throughs)
- Credits: unused committed capacity converts to credits; credits may roll forward up to 2 future quarters; maximum roll-forward per quarter = 50% of unused credit (operational cap)
- Burst protection: first 90 days after signature, overages billed at paygo minus 20% (softened overage) to give breathing room for initial spikes
- Step-up: if 4-week trailing usage > 85% of commit for two consecutive weeks, AeroCart may elect to increase commit to next tier. If they do, the higher unit price is guaranteed for 12 months from the step-up effective date.

Operational notes:
- Invoicing: credits will be applied as a line-item credit on the invoice (not a cash refund). David and finance will produce a sample invoice layout before signature.
- Legal: we’ll attach the draft SOW (attached) and route a short amendment with the credit language. Expect minor redlines — happy to pre-clear the standard clauses.

Next steps:
1) If procurement is comfortable with these terms, please reply and I’ll generate the DocuSign packet (SOW + amendment).
2) If you want a short run-through of the billing model, I can schedule a 30-min call with Kimberly and David this week.
